title: $27,000 in Student Loans Can Cost You $44,800
summary: Theo clicks accept all on his aid offer in four minutes; Ava spends two hours on hers. Theo ends up with the smaller monthly payment and still pays back about $12,700 more. This video explains seven things to understand before you sign: free money first (the 2027-28 FAFSA is already open), subsidized vs unsubsidized loans, interest that starts before your first bill, paying the interest while in school, the loan fee, borrowing less than you are offered, and how the new standard plan stretches bigger balances to 15 years, plus honesty checks on private loans and the catches. Examples assume the 2026-27 undergraduate rate of 6.52% for all four years, each year's loan sent out at the start of the school year, a six-month grace period, and a dependent student who qualifies for the full subsidized amount; they are illustrations, not predictions. Theo and Ava are fictional composites.
